scriptwriter.title: Scriptwriter
scriptwriter.role: Writes a 45-55 second script in the target language(s) with a 3-second hook, scene-by-scene visuals and on-screen text.

visual_producer.title: Visual Producer

options.label: 1. The Doorframe Arm Glitch
options.detail:
An interactive physical glitch where the viewer presses their arms against a doorframe for 30 seconds; when they step away, their arms float up involuntarily. This forces high retention and a comment flood of 'It worked!' or 'My arms are possessed!'
Hook (en): Press your arms here for 30 seconds.
Why: Interactive physical challenges have the highest VVSA because viewers must stay to see the result. The Kohnstamm phenomenon is a reliable physiological reflex that feels like 'magic' to the uninitiated.

options.label: 2. The Peripheral Vision Blindness Test
options.detail:
A visual 'disappearing' glitch. Viewers stare at a central black dot while colored circles on the edges vanish in real-time. This triggers a loop-watch to verify if the circles actually disappeared or if the brain just 'deleted' them.
Hook (en): Your brain is deleting what you see.
Why: Visual illusions are high-retention 'pattern interrupts'. The Troxler Effect is a proven viral hook because it feels like a personal failure of the viewer's own biology, driving high engagement and shares.

options.label: 3. The Panic-Button Face Hack
options.detail:
A survival hack showing how splashing ice-cold water on your eyes and cheekbones instantly lowers your heart rate via the Mammalian Dive Reflex. Viewers are challenged to try it next time they feel stressed, driving 'save' and 'share' metrics.
Hook (en): Splash cold water here to stop panic.
Why: Bio-hacks regarding anxiety and heart rate control are currently trending on health-tech YouTube. This specific reflex is a 'hidden setting' in human biology that produces an immediate, measurable physical change.
